title: Gap-bridge idempotent reconstitutor for console usage analytics
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: We need a robust, idempotent reconstitutor process that fills gaps in console usage telemetry across heterogeneous event sources without duplicating downstream metrics. This ticket implements a shard-aware 'gap-bridge' operator that detects missing sequence ranges, assembles canonical event deltas from source-of-truth stores, performs idempotent writes to the analytics warehouse, and emits reconciliation markers for observability.

Background and motivation: Recent incidents showed duplicated rows and overcounting after naive replays across multiple ingestion tiers (edge proxies, gateway aggregators, SDK buffered uploads). Existing replay tooling focuses on windowed, chronological replays but lacks a small deterministic merge strategy when partial overlapping segments and transformed payloads are present. The console product team needs accurate per-token and per-route cost metrics for billing and SLOs; overstated usage has high business impact.

Goals:
- Provide a gap detection algorithm that is shard-aware and resilient to clock drift.
- Reconstruct canonical events by merging deltas in deterministic order (derived from event keys + vector of precedence: authoritative source > gateway > SDK).
- Ensure reconstitutor is idempotent: repeated runs against the same token ranges must not create duplicates or corrupt aggregates.
- Emit reconciliation artifacts (checksums, commit tokens) and pipeline metrics to the console dashboard for validation.
- Support partial rollbacks and resumable progress markers so long backfills do not need a full restart.

Acceptance criteria:
1) End-to-end run on staging backfill dataset produces identical aggregates to golden dataset after two independent runs (bit-identical reconciliation markers).
2) No duplicate event rows in warehouse after reconstitutor run (validated via unique-event hash query).
3) Full observability: per-shard progress, write counters, dedupe rate, and reconciliation checksum exposed to the Console.
4) Can resume from the last commit token after a coordinator restart.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Chose deterministic precedence ordering instead of probabilistic heuristics to simplify idempotency proofs, at cost of requiring source annotations for priority.
- Use a lightweight commit token stored in Redis for short-term resumability and also periodically checkpoint to durable metadata in the metadata DB for long-running backfills. This duplicates state briefly but keeps recovery fast.
- Avoided fully stateful streaming replayer (which would be complex to maintain) and instead built a modular batch reconstitutor that can be layered on top of existing replay coordinator.

Implementation plan:
1) Implement shard-aware gap scanner: reads per-shard sequence watermarks and emits gap ranges (proto: gap.start,gap.end,shard).
2) Delta assembler: fetches raw records from sources (S3 event dumps, gateway change logs, SDK buffered uploads), normalizes schema, and sorts by (sequence, source precedence).
3) Idempotent writer: computes a deterministic event-hash and performs upsert semantics in the warehouse using merge keys. Writer also emits reconciliation checksum for the processed range.
4) Checkpointing and resume: store commit token per gap-range in Redis + metadata DB.
5) Observability: instrumentation hooks that export metrics and commit tokens to console.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for delta-merge ordering, hash collisions, and resume behaviour.
- Integration test in staging that runs the reconstitutor twice against the same gap list and asserts identical reconciliation markers and no duplicate rows.
- Load test with synthetic multi-shard gaps to measure throughput and memory usage.

Rollout plan:
- Canary runs on low-traffic customer shard in staging.
- Gradual run on 5% of historical gaps for a week; monitor dedupe rate and reconciliation checksum stability.
- Enable broad backfills once metrics are stable across 24h.

Rollback and mitigation:
- We can revert to snapshot materialized aggregates and use reconciliation markers to detect divergence. If corruption is detected, pause writes and run a targeted reconstitutor in read-only mode to produce a diff report.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Console/Gap-Bridge+Design (draft)
- Staging runbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/console/backfill-runbook.md
- Example PR (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1829
- Dashboard for reconciliation: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/backfill-reconciliation

Open questions:
- Do we require strict source annotations for precedence on all historical data? (PM prefers best-effort; engineering prefers strict). We chose to require annotations for new pipelines and best-effort heuristics for legacy data.
- Memory vs throughput trade-offs for in-memory sort of delta window; tuning required for very large gaps.

Notes: This ticket intentionally decouples deterministic merge logic from streaming replayers to maximize reuse and minimize blast radius during early rollout.
comments: 2026-01-19 - Liam Patel: Initial spike complete. Prototype delta assembler can normalize S3 and gateway logs; observed 0.002% hash collisions on synthetic dataset. Next: implement commit tokens.

2026-01-25 - Ava Chen: Feedback from PM (Maya Singh) - emphasize rolling checkpoints and add reconciliation dashboard panels before canary. Added 'reconciliation' metrics to labels and acceptance criteria.

2026-01-28 - Maya Singh: Design review: acceptable to use best-effort precedence for legacy data but needs clear annotation in logs when order is uncertain. PM requests visibility into events flagged as 'precedence-unknown'.

2026-02-02 - Liam Patel: Implemented idempotent writer using deterministic event-hash + MERGE on warehouse. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1829. Running integration tests in staging.

2026-02-08 - SRE (Noah Williams): Load test showed memory spike when assembling large contiguous gaps; added streaming sort fallback and bounded buffer approach. Updated implementation notes and estimate bumped from 5 to 8.
2026-02-11 - Liam Patel: Checkpointing added with Redis commit tokens and durable snapshots to metadata DB. Integration staging run passed the two-run idempotency test. Preparing canary run ticket.
